title: The Library Card
story: Daniel wanted a book about rivers for a school report, so he went to the college library after class. The reading room was quiet, and students sat at long tables. Meera, the librarian, stood behind the front desk with a stamp in her hand. Daniel searched the shelves and found a blue book with clear maps. Meera asked for his library card. Daniel checked his jacket pocket, then his bag, and then the pocket again. The card was not there. He remembered leaving it on his desk at home that morning. Without the card he could not borrow the book, and the report was due on Friday. Meera saw that he was worried. She asked his name and looked at the computer. His record was clean, and he had no late books. She said he could take the book for one night if he brought the card the next day. She wrote his name on a small slip and tucked the slip inside the cover. That evening he read the chapter about rivers and wrote three pages of notes. He put the library card into his bag before he went to bed so he would not forget it. In the morning he returned to the desk, showed the card, and Meera stamped the book in the normal way. Daniel learned that a careful librarian can help, but a card still belongs in your bag.
